answer: Each agent identity must first solve a unique computational puzzle bound to its public key before it can trade, like carving a distinct walnut shell pattern that cannot be copied. Difficulty scales with how many identities one operator holds, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real compute and time. A shared registry records each solved cipher challenge, like stamping a marble with a one-of-a-kind seal, letting peers reject duplicates cheaply while honest newcomers pay only once.
